Requirement: The cluster shall enter the ACTIVE state within 1.5 s of IGN changing from OFF to ON.
When IGN changes from ON to OFF, the cluster shall display the goodbye screen for 3 s.
After displaying the goodbye screen, the cluster shall enter the SLEEP state.
In the SLEEP state, the cluster shall draw no more than 0.1 mA from the battery supply.
The cluster should wake up quickly when a door is opened.
The cluster shall display vehicle speed received in the VehicleSpeed signal, in km/h or mph according to the unit setting.
The displayed speed shall never be lower than the actual vehicle speed.
The displayed speed shall not exceed the actual vehicle speed by more than 10 percent plus 4 km/h.
The displayed speed value shall be updated at least every 100 ms.
The cluster shall display engine speed from the EngineSpeed signal as a needle on a scale from 0 to 8000 rpm.
The red zone of the tachometer scale shall start at the value given by the configuration parameter RedlineRpm.
The cluster shall display the fuel level as a bar graph with eight segments.
The fuel level display shall be filtered so that it does not fluctuate when the vehicle is driving on an incline.
When the fuel level is below 10 percent, the low-fuel telltale shall be lit.
When BrakeWarn = 1, the cluster shall show the red brake system warning telltale steady on.
When BeltUnfastened = 1 and vehicle speed is above 20 km/h, the cluster shall flash the red seat belt reminder telltale at 1 Hz.
When FuelLow = 1, the cluster shall show the amber low fuel telltale steady on.
When MIL = 1, the cluster shall show the amber engine malfunction telltale steady on.
At each transition to the ACTIVE state, all telltales in Table 1 shall be lit for 2 s as a bulb check.
Red telltales shall have priority over amber telltales.
A telltale whose input signal has not been received for more than 500 ms shall be lit.
When a telltale input signal has not been received for more than 500 ms, a DTC shall be stored.
The cluster shall play the seat belt chime while the seat belt reminder telltale is flashing.
The chime volume should be adequate for all driving conditions.
If two chimes are requested at the same time, the cluster shall play the chime with the higher priority as defined in the chime priority list.
The driver shall be able to scroll through the trip computer pages using the up and down buttons on the left steering wheel switch.
A long press of the OK button for more than 2 s shall reset the selected trip counter.
The cluster may offer a menu to change the display theme.
The cluster shall communicate on the powertrain CAN bus at a bit rate of 500 kbit/s.
If a CAN signal is not received within three times its cycle time, the cluster shall treat the signal as invalid.
The cluster shall transmit the ClusterStatus message every 100 ms.
After a bus-off event, the cluster shall attempt recovery as specified in the network management document.
The cluster shall store a DTC when the display backlight driver reports a fault.
Stored DTCs shall be readable by a diagnostic tester.
The cluster shall perform a display self-test at startup.
The cluster shall report the result of the display self-test.
The cluster software shall be updatable through the diagnostic connector.
A software update shall be accepted only if its digital signature is valid.
If an update fails, the cluster shall return to the previously installed software version.
Diagnostic services that write memory shall require successful security access authentication.
The cluster shall protect cryptographic keys appropriately.
The cluster shall detect a mismatch between the displayed and requested state of the brake system warning telltale within 200 ms.
If a brake system warning telltale mismatch is detected, the cluster shall display a text warning.
The cluster shall display the first frame within 2 s of power-up.
The graphics shall run smoothly at all times.
CPU load shall not exceed 70 percent averaged over any 1 s window.
